Welded into the floor plates at the trench's wide end, a single smooth ivory arch of rib rises twice a minifigure height, wide enough to walk two figures under side by side, a soft brush laid along its top ridge; the flat tan plate floor runs right up to its base and continues past on both sides unbroken.

Sunk into the ochre band halfway up the cut face, one colossal LEGO brick sits proud of the wall with its studs the size of tabletops, a tin bucket hooked over the nearest corner stud; the wall courses close over its far end and run on unbroken to both frame edges.

Held in the floor at the near end of the trench, a giant iron key lies flat with its bow as tall as a standing minifigure and its teeth as long as a ladder rung, a folded canvas draped over the bow; the swept tile floor runs up to it and past it as one unbroken surface.

Set into the dark charcoal band low in the trench wall, a great pale cheek of smooth brick shows one closed eye above the floor line, as wide as the ladder is tall, moss tufts grown along the brow and a rope sling looped under the chin; the wall courses run straight across it on both sides unbroken.

Resting in the floor across the middle of the trench, a blunt jaw lies level with blocky white teeth standing up in a row, the tallest tooth level with a minifigure's chest, a round sieve with a mesh bottom balanced across the jawline; the flat plate floor runs up against it and continues past on both sides.

Grown across with brown flexible-tube roots where it meets the cut face, a fin of trans-blue plates stands up out of the floor with a row of round ports along its ridge, taller than the ladder leaning nearby, a rumpled tarpaulin weighted at its base with grey stones; the floor plates run right up to it unbroken and carry on past.

Welded into the floor plates beneath the spoil heap end, one enormous cog stands up in a quarter circle with three teeth clear of the floor and each tooth taller than a crew figure, a folded canvas draped over the highest tooth and loose tan studs heaped against the rim; the swept tile floor runs up to it and on past unbroken.

Sunk into the red band near the trench floor, the prow of an enormous vessel curves up out of the plates in a single sweeping wedge as tall as three ladder rungs, a coil of rope looped over its tip and a wicker basket set against its flank; the floor plates run right up to it and continue past on both sides.

Set into the pale sandy band midway up the cut, one enormous anchor fluke juts up from the wall in a broad curved horn as tall as the tent ridge behind the crew, a plank walkway resting across its widest point; the wall courses close over its base and run on to the frame edges as one unbroken surface.

Held in the floor at the trench's far end, a golden minifigure head the size of a garden hut sits with its printed smile above the plate line, its top stud wider than two figures lying end to end, a wicker basket heaped with potsherds resting against one cheek; the flat plate floor runs up to it and past on both sides as one unbroken surface.

Resting in the floor along the trench's long wall, a spread of finger bones each the length of a plank lies flat with the knuckle arch standing as high as a minifigure waist, a canvas sack slumped and half-full draped over the highest knuckle; the tile floor runs right up to the bones and continues past them unbroken.

Welded into the floor plates at the trench centre, a great wheel rim stands up in a quarter circle as tall as the ladder, its curved edge of dark iron rising clean above the plates, a tin bucket hooked over its highest point and loose tan studs heaped against its inner face; the floor runs up to it and past on both sides unbroken.

Grown across with brown flexible-tube roots from the cut face, one coiled shell the size of the crew tent sits with its outer whorl clear of the floor and its spiral ridge taller than any standing figure, a soft brush resting in the groove of the outermost coil; the swept tile floor runs right up to it and continues past on both sides.

Sunk into the pale ochre band high in the cut face, a robot's forearm of grey brick juts from the wall with three finger joints open and each finger as long as a ladder rung, a coil of rope draped over the lowest open joint; the wall courses close over the elbow end and run on to the frame edge unbroken.

Set into the floor plates at the trench's near end, a hatch of dark plate sits flush with a great wheel handle at its centre as wide as two figures standing apart, three crew figures seated along the rim eating, their feet dangling over the plate seam; the flat tile floor runs right up to the hatch edge and carries on past as one unbroken surface.

Held in the floor across the middle of the trench, a stair of wide pale brick descends into the floor between the plate courses, warm amber light rising up from below between the steps, a wicker basket with a dipper hooked over its rim set on the topmost step; the swept plate floor runs up to the stair head and continues past on both sides unbroken.

Resting in the floor beneath the ladder end, a single enormous tusk curves up out of the plates in one clean arc, its tip reaching as high as the tent ridge and its base as wide as three figures side by side, a rope sling looped around its midpoint and a tin bucket resting in the curve; the tile floor runs up to it and past on both sides unbroken.

Welded into the floor plates at the spoil end, a splayed claw lies with three curved toes pointing up, the longest toe standing as high as a minifigure chest, a round sieve with a mesh bottom resting across two of the toes; the flat tan plate floor runs right up to the claw base and continues past on both sides as one unbroken surface.

Sunk into the dark charcoal band at the trench base, a great bell of pale smooth brick sits with its lip clear of the floor and its crown as wide as the ladder is long, a plank walkway bridging the open mouth and a canvas sack slumped against the outer curve; the wall courses run up to it and past on both sides as one unbroken surface.

Set into the red ochre band halfway up the cut face, one enormous knobbled vertebra of white curved slopes and arch bricks sits proud of the wall, taller than a figure and as wide as three ladder rungs, a soft brush laid along its top ridge and loose tan studs heaped at its foot; the wall courses close over its far side and run on to the frame edge unbroken.

Grown across with brown flexible-tube roots along its upper edge, a stepped mosaic floor of coloured tiles runs out from under the trench wall in a broad flat band two plank-lengths wide, its tile pattern clear and its far edge pressing up against the smooth tan plate floor; the tan plates run up to the mosaic edge and carry straight on past it as one unbroken surface.

Held in the floor at the wide end of the trench, the flat pan of a colossal shoulder blade of smooth white plate lies level with its raised spine standing up from the surface as high as a minifigure waist, a folded tarpaulin weighted with grey stones draped over the spine; the swept tile floor runs right up to the blade edge and continues past on both sides unbroken.

Welded into the floor plates at the trench's near end, a giant tap of dark-grey brick stands up with its spout as high as the tent ridge, its body wider than two figures standing side by side, a coil of rope looped around the base of the spout and a tin bucket set beneath it; the flat plate floor runs up to the tap base and past on both sides as one unbroken surface.

Resting in the floor beneath the cut face, a great hand of white brick lies palm-open, each finger as long as a plank and the thumb standing up as high as a minifigure chest, a shallow puddle of trans-blue plates standing in the open palm; the flat tile floor runs right up to the wrist edge and continues past on both sides as one unbroken surface.

Set into the pale sandy band low in the trench wall, a giant ladder built for something far larger than any crew figure pokes from the cut face with four rungs clear of the floor, each rung as long as a plank and as thick as a barrel, a canvas sack tied with cord hanging from the highest visible rung; the wall courses run across it on both sides and carry on to the frame edge unbroken.
